phase2: Tiens, tiens… Tu as marqué un point. Have you ever been this lucky before? Je ne crois pas !
Hmm. Tu progresses. You're better than I thought… mais toujours pas as good as me !
Je n'ai jamais, never, au grand jamais raté une question. Et ce n'est pas aujourd'hui que je vais commencer !
phase3: ASSEZ ! J'ai corrigé des millions de copies, and I have NEVER lost my temper… jusqu'à aujourd'hui !
Tu vas voir ce que tu vas voir ! I'm going to give you the hardest questions in the world !
Je bouillonne depuis cinq minutes ! I have been angry FOR five minutes, pas SINCE five minutes, note-le bien !
lose: Échec ! Mais tu as essayé, isn't it ? … Pardon : haven't you ? Tu vois, même moi, je suis presque parfait.
Reviens quand tu auras révisé. When you HAVE revised, pas « when you will have revised » !
Tu as perdu ? So have many others. Allez, au tableau, et cent lignes de present perfect !

questions.q: Look at those black clouds! It ___ rain any minute.
questions.explain: On VOIT la preuve (les nuages noirs) : be going to pour une prédiction évidente.

questions.q: Oh no, I forgot my wallet! — Don't worry, I ___ for your lunch.
questions.explain: Décision prise sur le coup, pour rendre service : will + base verbale.

questions.q: Comment dit-on « Quand je serai à la retraite, je vivrai au bord d'un lac » ?
choices: When I will retire, I will live by a lake.
When I retire, I live by a lake.
When I retire, I will live by a lake.
When I will retire, I live by a lake.
questions.explain: Après when, présent (When I retire) ; dans l'autre partie, le futur avec will.

questions.q: We ___ my cousins at the airport at six tomorrow. The tickets are booked.
questions.explain: Rendez-vous fixé (heure, billets) : présent continu, we are meeting.

questions.q: I promise I ___ eat the last cookie again.
questions.explain: Promesse au négatif : won't (= will not) + base verbale.

questions.q: Call me when you ___ at the cottage.
questions.explain: Après when, on parle du futur avec le présent : when you arrive, jamais when you will arrive.

questions.q: Grandma has bought new skis: she ___ learn to ski at seventy!
questions.explain: Projet déjà décidé (elle a acheté les skis) : be going to + base verbale.

questions.q: Take an umbrella. According to the forecast, it ___ rainy all afternoon.
questions.explain: Prédiction de la météo : will + be, sans to et sans -s.

questions.q: Dad ___ his famous chili for the neighbours on Saturday. He has already invited them.
questions.explain: Plan organisé (les invitations sont faites) : présent continu, is cooking.

questions.q: It's going to snowing tonight, so wear your toque.
questions.explain: Be going to + base verbale : going to snow, sans -ing.

questions.q: We'll leave when Mom finish her coffee.
questions.explain: Après when, présent simple : Mom = she, donc finishes avec -es.

questions.q: Don't worry, I will helps you with your science project.
questions.explain: Après will, toujours la base verbale : will help, jamais de -s.

questions.q: My little sister is ___ than me at video games, and she never lets me forget it.
questions.explain: Good est irrégulier : good, better, the best. Jamais more good ni gooder.

questions.q: This is ___ pizza I have ever eaten. Never again!
questions.explain: Superlatif irrégulier de bad : the worst, avec the.

questions.q: Our new apartment isn't ___ the old one.
questions.explain: « Aussi… que » = as + adjectif simple + as. Au négatif : isn't as big as.

questions.q: Comment dit-on « Le chalet est plus loin que le lac » ?
choices: The cottage is more far than the lake.
The cottage is farer that the lake.
The cottage is far than the lake.
The cottage is farther than the lake.
questions.explain: Far est irrégulier : far, farther, the farthest. Et « que » = than.

questions.q: Today is ___ day of the year: minus thirty-five degrees!
questions.explain: Adjectif court : the + -est, the coldest.

questions.q: This math problem is ___ than the last one.
questions.explain: Adjectif long : more + adjectif + than.

questions.q: My cat is ___ than my dog, and he knows it.
questions.explain: Adjectif court d'une syllabe : smart → smarter.

questions.q: The traffic was ___ than yesterday, so we were late again.
questions.explain: Comparatif irrégulier : bad → worse → the worst.

questions.q: Our street is the ___ in the whole neighbourhood, thanks to Mr. Patel's rooster.
questions.explain: Consonne + y : le y devient i, puis -est : noisiest.

questions.q: My grandpa is older that my grandma.
questions.explain: Dans une comparaison, « que » se dit than, pas that.

questions.q: This is the hotest summer in years.
questions.explain: Hot est court et finit par consonne-voyelle-consonne : on double le t, hottest.

questions.q: My brother is as tall than my dad now.
questions.explain: « Aussi grand que » = as tall as : as… as, jamais as… than.

questions.q: ___ you ever ridden a camel?
questions.explain: Expérience de vie avec ever : present perfect, Have you ever + participe passé.

questions.q: Where's Karim? — He has ___ to the dentist. He'll be back at noon.
questions.explain: Il est parti et il n'est pas encore revenu : has gone. Has been voudrait dire qu'il est déjà revenu.

questions.q: Comment dit-on « Je n'ai jamais vu d'aurores boréales » ?
choices: I haven't never seen the northern lights.
I have never saw the northern lights.
I have never seen the northern lights.
I didn't never see the northern lights.
questions.explain: Une seule négation (never) + participe passé (seen) : I have never seen.

questions.q: How many times have you ___ on a plane?
questions.explain: Participe passé de fly : flown (fly, flew, flown).

questions.q: Have you ever ___ a horse on the beach?
questions.explain: Participe passé irrégulier : ride, rode, ridden.

questions.q: My uncle has ___ the same joke at every family dinner.
questions.explain: Present perfect = have / has + participe passé : tell, told, told.

questions.q: I've ___ swum in the Atlantic Ocean. Is it really that cold?
questions.explain: « Jamais » avec un verbe affirmatif : I've never swum.

questions.q: My parents have ___ to Japan twice, and they want to go back.
questions.explain: Ils y sont allés et en sont revenus : have been to.

questions.q: Chloé has ___ to make Grandma's tourtière three times, but it's never as good.
questions.explain: Try → tried : consonne + y devient -ied.

questions.q: Have you ever eat poutine with maple syrup on it?
questions.explain: Après have, le participe passé : eat, ate, eaten.

questions.q: I have ever met a famous hockey player.
questions.explain: Ever ne s'emploie pas dans une phrase affirmative de ce type : I have never met.

questions.q: My sister has broke her arm twice on her skateboard.
questions.explain: Participe passé de break : broken (break, broke, broken).

questions.q: We have lived in Gatineau ___ I was five.
questions.explain: I was five est un point de départ : since.

questions.q: Comment dit-on « Je connais Léa depuis trois ans » ?
choices: I have known Léa for three years.
I know Léa since three years.
I have known Léa since three years.
I am knowing Léa for three years.
questions.explain: Situation qui dure encore : present perfect (have known) + for devant une durée.

questions.q: Have you cleaned your room ___?
questions.explain: Yet se place à la fin d'une question ou d'une négation.

questions.q: I ___ my keys yesterday, and I still can't find them.
questions.explain: Yesterday est un moment précis du passé : passé simple, lost.

questions.q: How long ___ you known your best friend?
questions.explain: How long + present perfect : How long have you known… ?

questions.q: No dessert for me, thanks. I ___ eaten a huge lunch.
questions.explain: « Je viens de » = I have just + participe passé.

questions.q: My neighbour has played the bagpipes every morning ___ June. Help!
questions.explain: June est un point de départ : since June.

questions.q: We've been stuck in this lineup ___ forty minutes.
questions.explain: Forty minutes est une durée : for forty minutes.

questions.q: My grandparents ___ married for fifty years.
questions.explain: Ils sont toujours mariés : present perfect de be, have been + for.

questions.q: I am at this school since grade seven.
questions.explain: « Je suis ici depuis » = present perfect : I have been at this school since grade seven.

questions.q: He hasn't called me already.
questions.explain: Dans une phrase négative, « encore » se dit yet, à la fin : He hasn't called me yet.

questions.q: My dad has had this old car since twelve years.
questions.explain: Twelve years est une durée : for twelve years, jamais since.

questions.q: You've met my cousin before, ___?
questions.explain: La phrase est au present perfect (you've met) : on reprend have au négatif, haven't you?

questions.q: I'm on the right bus, ___?
questions.explain: Cas spécial : avec I am, le tag est aren't I?

questions.q: I can't stand cold pizza. — ___
questions.explain: Phrase négative : Neither + auxiliaire positif + sujet. Pas de double négation.

questions.q: Your brother never cleans his room, ___?
questions.explain: Never rend la phrase négative : le tag est positif, does he?

questions.q: Mom loves maple fudge, and so ___ Dad.
questions.explain: Présent simple positif : so + does + sujet (Dad = he).

questions.q: That movie was amazing, ___ it?
questions.explain: Phrase positive avec was : tag négatif, wasn't it?

questions.q: They won't forget the cake, ___ they?
questions.explain: Phrase négative avec won't : tag positif, will they?

questions.q: Did you lock the front door? — Yes, I ___.
questions.explain: Réponse courte : on reprend l'auxiliaire de la question, Yes, I did.

questions.q: Your parents went to Halifax last summer, ___ they?
questions.explain: Passé simple sans auxiliaire : on prend did, au négatif, didn't they?

questions.q: You speak Spanish, doesn't you?
questions.explain: Avec you, l'auxiliaire est do : don't you?

questions.q: I didn't sleep well last night. Me too.
questions.explain: Après une phrase négative, « moi non plus » = Me neither, jamais Me too.

questions.q: Liam has already eaten, hasn't Liam?
questions.explain: Dans le tag, on remplace le nom par un pronom : hasn't he?
